about: T-3959: real asks the user made, each with the row Sampo already held that should have caught it (a catcher id from pool) or null when nothing held it. split is train or held: every third row (index 2, 5, 8, ...) is held out, scored but never used to set COS_MIN. cos is the bge-m3 cosine of the ask to its catcher row (to the nearest pool row when the catcher is null), measured once with plugin/lib/sampo/selfaware.py's own pool text; the stem path (no embedder) is what the test scores. A closed user ask adds one row at the end: its text, its catcher from a human reading, the next split in the cycle, and its cos from one embedder run; then the floor below is re-recorded. Caveats: recall and top are pool-size dependent (the live pool holds hundreds of briefs and verbs; the pool here is 20 real rows padded with distractor briefs and verbs to 80, so a catcher no longer lands in the 8 just by sharing a key), and floor.top counts catchers ranked first, not merely in the 8; floor.pool is the least pool size the test accepts. The held split is not clean for the stem path: the 'skills ... been used' row (index 2, held) is one of the three named misses the USE_FORMS/_stems fix was written for, so its held recall measures that fix, not generalisation; held rows from asks nobody tuned for (the next added asks) should stay held for the stem path until a fix is written for them. A themed catcher (an ask and row that share a THEMES stem) skips the cosine gate, so its cos row (index 1, .567 under COS_MIN) is scored by the gate column as wrong on purpose.

Hook timeouts retry once when the machine is under load

Dashboard page shows queue depth, blocked tasks and lane count per project

Docs impact line on every brief names the README sections a change touches
Version bump script updates the plugin manifest and the marketplace entry together
Secrets scanner blocks a commit that holds a token shaped string

Night mode runs the queue headless with a spend cap and a stop file

Search ranks verbs by stem overlap and prefers the rarer words

Pane panels redraw only the rows that changed to keep the terminal calm
Decisions are logged with a default and surfaced in the final report
Research shelf keeps cited answers with the date they were found
Lint gate runs the formatter check on changed files only
Capture command files discovered work and marks urgent ones
Plugin install verb finds a missing capability and pins the chosen one
Windows paths are normalised in the scope check so a backslash still matches

Budget verb caps the tokens a subagent may spend per task

next: close the finished task and start the next queued one
status: a short summary of where work stands and what is left
queue: list the queued tasks in their run order
capture: file a new request or a discovered piece of work as a task
checkpoint: save the task state before switching or a risky step
pause: stop the running work and wait
intake: parse a block of tagged lines into tasks
ideas: a grounded brainstorm where lens agents read the code
review: five lens review of a diff with skeptics refuting each finding
research: find out what exists and what to reuse with cited answers
release: gate the commit, bump the version, write the changelog and tag
budget: cap the spend of subagents and show what is used
profile: show or set the machine local preferences
sync: keep tasks with the repository
drive: continue open work automatically when a turn ends
sensitive: mark a repository so nothing leaves the machine
plugins: find, pin and install a missing capability
outline: list the functions and classes of a file with line numbers
find: rank the leads in an unfamiliar repository
prove: show a lead red with a failing test before fixing it
gates: name the audits a task needs before it is done
check: run the lint, type and test gates on the change
decide: record a decision with its default and review the costly ones
run: work the queue headless
which: tell which verb does a thing
